intro: This week’s digest highlights strategic moves reshaping retail and AI sectors, including Target’s launch of a digital-twin platform to enhance inventory management and Kroger’s appointment of a former Walmart executive to lead e-commerce transformation. In AI, Anthropic reports a significant revenue surge, while OpenAI undergoes executive changes amid ongoing industry consolidation, exemplified by Silver Lake’s reported takeover talks with Workday.

readOneThing.title: Target builds digital-twin platform to improve inventory availability

items.title: Target builds digital-twin platform to improve inventory availability
bullets: Target developed Proxima, an in-house digital twin platform, to simulate and optimize inventory flow from regional distribution centers to stores.
A pilot test with 63 fresh food items using Proxima improved on-shelf availability by 2.5% through simulated inventory adjustments.
Proxima supports Target's broader supply chain modernization efforts, including launching a new receive center in Houston for seasonal and bulky items.
items.summary: AI-generated summary: Target has launched a digital-twin platform aimed at enhancing inventory availability in its stores, reflecting its ongoing efforts to improve stock levels.

items.title: Workday shares post best day in 10 years on Silver Lake takeover report
bullets: Workday's shares surged nearly 18% following reports that private equity firm Silver Lake is in talks to acquire the company. The stock's market value closed at nearly $51 billion after multiple trading halts during the surge. In March 2026, co-founder Aneel Bhusri was reinstated as CEO amid ongoing concerns about AI's impact on the software business model.

items.title: Anthropic revenue reportedly jumps to more than $11.5 billion in second quarter
bullets: Anthropic reported preliminary revenue exceeding $11.5 billion in the second quarter, marking a significant increase from the previous year. The company's revenue surged more than 14-fold compared to $787 million in the same quarter last year and rose from $4.73 billion in the first quarter of 2026. Anthropic is preparing for a potential initial public offering as early as this fall, aiming to become one of the first major private AI companies to enter public markets.
The AI company reported preliminary revenue of more than $11.5 billion for its latest completed quarter, up from $787 million in the same period last year, documents viewed by Bloomberg showed

items.title: The Customer Identity And Access Management Solutions Landscape, Q3 2026 Is Live
bullets: Forrester published the 2026 report on customer identity and access management (CIAM) solutions, identifying AI agents as a new identity type in the landscape.
CIAM solutions now include digital worker functionality that assists with migration, A/B testing, threat detection, and fraud management.
A new Forrester Wave evaluation on CIAM is scheduled for late September 2026, updating the previous report from December 2024.

items.title: OpenAI hires new CRO as executive shake-up continues
bullets: OpenAI appointed Dali Rajic, former Wiz president and COO, as its new chief revenue officer following Denise Dresser's nine-month tenure.
The company has over one billion weekly active users and serves two million businesses, but has not met all of its revenue targets.
Recent executive departures include COO Brad Lightcap and AGI deployment CEO Fidji Simo, with co-founder Greg Brockman taking on expanded management duties.

items.title: Silver Lake in talks to buy Workday, sources say
bullets: Private equity firm Silver Lake has engaged in confidential discussions to potentially acquire Workday, a human-resources and financial management software company. Workday's workforce in India has grown to approximately 1,300 employees across Mumbai and two other cities, with plans to expand further. The ongoing talks could result in one of the largest software buyouts in history, as Workday's market value stands around $43 billion amid a significant stock decline this year.

items.title: Kroger names former Walmart executive as first e-commerce chief
bullets: Kroger appointed Nate Faust, a former Walmart executive and Jet.com co-founder, as its first executive vice president and chief e-commerce officer starting September 1.
In the most recent quarter, Kroger's e-commerce operations achieved profitability for the first time, with online sales growing 19% year-over-year driven by delivery services.

This leadership change follows Kroger's recent CEO appointment of Greg Foran, another Walmart veteran, and occurs amid Kroger's strategic focus on enhancing its digital business and store-based fulfillment.
items.summary: AI-generated summary: Kroger has appointed Nate Faust, a former Walmart executive, as its first e-commerce chief, following the recent naming of another Walmart veteran, Greg Foran, as CEO. This move highlights Kroger's focus on strengthening its digital and e-commerce leadership.
